items.title: Daredevil Star Charlie Cox Confirms He's in an Unannounced Sega Game | NYCC 2026
items.excerpt: Daredevil star Charlie Cox has confirmed that he is starring in another video game, this one for Sega.
items.content_text: Daredevil star Charlie Cox has confirmed that he is starring in another video game, this one for Sega. Cox opened up about the project at New York Comic-Con 2026, telling IGN’s Jeffrey Vega that he’s completed recording for an as-yet unannounced Sega video game. “I did another one! It doesn’t have a name yet,” he said. “I did a Sega one. I’ve done one since. It hasn’t come out yet. It was fun to do. It’s hard. It’s a whole different job, man.” Cox went on to share a humorous anecdote about his experience working on the game, saying that the crew weren’t aware that he wasn’t American. “I’m not sure what I’m allowed to say, but I showed up for it, and I met them for the first time, they asked me to do this game, and so I agreed to it. Then I had to do 40 hours or whatever it was, and I showed up for the first day, and I was like, ‘Hi guys, nice to meet you! How are you?’ And all of them went, ‘...oh, he’s English.’ They’d hoped, they’d wanted him to be American. But now I’ve got to do 40 hours of lines I’ve not prepared in an accent. Yeah, I think they thought I was American.” This, at least, gives us one bit of information about his role in the mysterious game — he’ll be playing an American character (or at least, a character with an American accent), and it’s likely that his role will be central to the plot, given that he recorded 40 hours’ worth of lines for it. It's also worth noting that Cox confirmed he was working on a new game earlier this year, though he similarly declined to mention many details at the time. Thus far, that’s all we know. Cox has already proven his voice acting chops with Expedition 33 , where he played Gustave, famously recording all of his lines in a mere four-hour session. Players lauded his performance after the game released in 2025, and he was even nominated for Best Performance at the Game Awards that year. Sega’s upcoming lineup of video game releases includes Stranger Than Heaven , Virtua Fighter Crossroads , Persona 6 , and Alien: Isolation 2 , among several others. Given that this particular project doesn’t even have a name yet, it’s unlikely that it’s any of these that have already been announced, so we’ll just have to wait and see what’s in store. In the meantime, fans of Charlie Cox can look forward to Daredevil: Born Again Season 3, though this is set to be the end of Matt Murdock’s current adventures — at least for the time being. The news broke in late September alongside reports that its showrunner, Dario Scardapane, exited the series while it was in post-production. Kingpin actor Vincent D’Onofrio penned a heartfelt goodbye to the series on social media, writing, “We have the final Season, season 3 heading your way next year with some very cool stuff. Much love to all who have been supportive. I love that character Fisk. Always will. Off to another neck off the woods. Meanwhile… Season 3 is coming!” Daredevil Born Again: Season 3 is set to release in early 2027. Image Credits: Arturo Holmes/Getty Images for Disney

items.title: Charlie Cox on the Return of The Defenders — 'There Needed to Be Some Kind of Closure' | NYCC 2026
items.excerpt: Charlie Cox is telling fans to "get the Save Daredevil Campaign" going as Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 will be the show's last.
items.content_text: Charlie Cox hit New York Comic Con today to join in the Marvel Television panel — jetlagged and just in from Dublin, but ready to talk the return of Daredevil for Season 3 of Born Again. And not just the return of the Horned One, but also his old teammates The Defenders. "I think there needed to be a full circle with that story," Cox told IGN's Jeffrey Vega today after the panel. "There needed to be some kind of closure with it." The Defenders of course originated in the Netflix Marvel era, where each character — Daredevil, Jessica Jones (Krysten Ritter), Luke Cage (Mike Colter), and Iron Fist (Finn Jones) — had their own series before teaming up for the 2017 Defenders season. Eventually those shows all came to an end, but when Cox and Vincent D'Onofrio showed up in the proper MCU, it seemed like only a matter of time before the street-level heroes would be reunited. Charlie Cox, Finn Jones, and Krysten Ritter reunite on the #NYCC stage! #Daredevil https://t.co/XUJ200rP8w — Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) October 8, 2026 "And Marvel were willing and able to bring them back and have a lot of fun with it," the actor said of the quartet returning. "It was great. We're such good friends. We have a great time together. There's some really interesting, fun dynamics that the fans seem to love, so it was great." Part of that fun, Cox joked, was Mike Colter "giving away spoilers non-stop" — referring of course to the actor putting some info on social earlier this year that he shouldn't have. "We had to ban him from getting sides on set!" As for whether or not Born Again Season 3, which has been confirmed to be the last season of the show, means we won't see Cox put on the horns again, the actor says it might be up to the fans to decide on that front. "Don't know, man. I don't know," he said when asked whether or not he's done as Daredevil. "I mean, it might be. It might be. Don't worry about Kevin [Feige]. Get the Save Daredevil campaign on the horn. Get them motivated. That engine, that won't stop until there's some resolution. That's my true superpower -- is the Save Daredevil campaign!"
items.title_en: Charlie Cox on the Return of The Defenders — 'There Needed to Be Some Kind of Closure' | NYCC 2026

items.title: Jay and Silent Bob’s Joint Venture Trailer and Game Details Revealed for Weed Farming Sim | NYCC 2026
items.excerpt: Jay and Silent Bob’s Joint Venture turns Kevin Smith’s View Askewniverse into a foul-mouthed cozy weed farming simulator. New details and the first trailer were revealed at New York Comic Con 2026.
items.content_text: Nitrate Games revealed the first footage and new details about its upcoming farm sim video game Jay and Silent Bob’s Joint Venture at New York Comic Con on Thursday. IGN can exclusively share the first trailer for the game, which you can watch via the player embedded below. Jay and Silent Bob’s Joint Venture promises a funny and raunchy spin on the cozy farming genre, with creator Kevin Smith’s iconic characters out to “build the best weed farm in town.” Players will build, cultivate and expand their operation, interact with familiar faces, and experience an original story written by Ernie Altbacker (the animated films Batman: Hush and Justice League Dark). Kevin Smith and Jason Mewes have been creative forces on the project from the start. “Since Jay and Silent Bob are the stars of this hilarious growing game, I cannot wait to play with myself!,” said Kevin Smith in a statement provided to IGN. “Many thanks to Nitrate Games for taking my little animals to this crossing and making them Stars Dew a Valley!” “Joint Venture is a Jay and Silent Bob game, but it’s actually a continuation of Kevin Smith’s View Askewniverse,” says Nitrate Games co-founder Montana Sommese. “The central narrative picks up where the films left off, making the game a kind of sequel. Players can befriend and engage with their favorite characters from Kevin Smith's movies like never before. As we update the game over time, we're excited to be able to expand Kevin's story universe with narrative updates that will continue building from his cinematic universe.” The NYCC panel revealed that other familiar faces from the View Askewniverse appear in the game, including Clerks’ Dante, Randal and Veronica; Mallrats’ Brodie and T.S. Quint; Chasing Amy’s Holden, Banky, Hooper and Alyssa; Dogma’s Azrael and Serendipity; Clerks II’s Becky & Elias; and Mooby. Jay and Silent Bob’s Joint Venture is currently heading toward its play testing phase of production, with an expected release in late Spring 2027 on Steam/PC. A console release is also slated for 2027. Fans can learn more and s ign up to playtest and wishlist.
items.title_en: Jay and Silent Bob’s Joint Venture Trailer and Game Details Revealed for Weed Farming Sim | NYCC 2026

items.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Premieres This Week — Here's When You Can Watch New Episodes
items.content_text: Avatar: Seven Havens premieres this week, introducing us to the first new Avatar in over 10 years. Original creators Michael Dante DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko returned for the 2D series, which follows a new Avatar, Pavi, over 200 years after The Legend of Korra. That’s around 300 years after the events of The Last Airbender. Seven Havens will be streaming exclusively on Paramount+, now under the Skydance banner . The full series is slated for 26 half-hour episodes, just like the good ol’ days. However, those episodes will be split into two “Books,” the Avatar version of seasons. Avatar: Seven Havens Book 1 Premieres This Week The first three episodes of Book 1 will premiere on October 9. Subsequent episodes will be released in batches every Friday, so all 13 episodes of the Seven Havens will be streaming by the end of October. Here’s how that all looks in list form: Avatar: Seven Havens Episode Release Schedule Chapter 1: “On the Horizon” - October 9 Chapter 2: “Into the Storm” - October 9 Chapter 3: “The Order” - October 9 Chapter 4: The Faceless” - October 16 Chapter 5: “The One Left Behind” - October 16 Chapter 6: “The Night of the Inflicted” - October 16 Chapter 7: “What Lies Beneath” - October 23 Chapter 8: “The Envoys, Part 1” - October 23 Chapter 9: “The Envoys, Part 2” - October 23 Chapter 10: “Ghosts and Spirits” - October 30 Chapter 11: “Battle of the Ruins” - October 30 Chapter 12: “The Dome” - October 30 Chapter 13: “The Root Chakra” - October 30 As mentioned, the series will be streaming exclusively on Paramount+. Previous Avatar shows have eventually been released on DVD and Blu-ray, but that seems less likely for Seven Havens in the current Paramount era. Episode titles were originally reported by Polygon , alongside promotional art for each batch: As for what to expect from the show, Seven Havens follows the usual Avatar tradition by picking up with, well, a new Avatar. The star of the new animated series is a young earthbender named Pavi. Korra picked up less than a century after The Last Airbender, entering an era of industrialization in an otherwise recognizable version of the Four Nations. Seven Havens, in contrast, jumps over 200 years into the future. Early trailers show an entirely distinct post-apocalyptic world that generally despises the notion of the Avatar. Given the amount of time that’s passed, it’s possible something happened to the Avatar Cycle to cause a delay in its continuation after Korra’s passing. Otherwise, Korra may have hit a Kyoshi-level lifespan. Either way, it seems like some real crazy stuff went down after Korra and Asami walked into the sunset . Paramount, which has completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. , has been rebuilding the Avatar franchise over the past couple of years. Most recently, Paramount dropped Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender, a new animated movie featuring the original Gaang all grown up. That was notoriously leaked online in protest of Paramount’s refusal to give it a theatrical release, but we were fans of the movie nonetheless. Otherwise, while Seven Havens has already been greenlit for 26 episodes, there’s no word on when we’ll actually see Book 2. We’ll likely hear more about the series’ future as well as other projects like the Avatar fighting game at NYCC this weekend. ICYMI: Reebok just announced a new line of sneakers inspired by the original ATLA series.

items.title: Animals Review
items.excerpt: The new Netflix thriller Animals is tautly directed by Ben Affleck, who keeps the emphasis on the characters’ flawed humanity. None of the choices available to the protagonists are good ones, and the many “what would you do in this scenario?” questions the film poses keep the story compelling when the kidnapping plot itself ventures into formula.
items.content_text: Animals is in select theaters and on Netflix on October 9. Ben Affleck is back behind and in front of the camera with Animals, an entertaining new thriller that spices up the kidnap movie formula with a neat twist that asks big moral questions of its protagonists and viewers. Affleck plays Mark Kimball, a tycoon running as an independent candidate to become the next mayor of Los Angeles. (It should be noted that LA is currently in a heated mayoral campaign, so kudos, Netflix, on the timing of your film’s release.) Mark is a middle-aged white male Army veteran with progressive views and a Black wife and mixed-race son, who takes no outside funding and speaks fluent Spanish. It’s a cynical political strategist’s dream candidate come true, something the film acknowledges. It’s Halloween and LA is just days away from electing its next mayor. Mark has run a vigorous, self-funded campaign, and yet he’s behind enough that he could lose the election and with it, all the fortune he’s poured into it. His therapist wife Abigail (Kerry Washington) doesn’t know the extent to which he’s spent their savings on his campaign. And what Mark doesn’t know about – but which was revealed in the trailer – is that Abigail is having an affair (the other man is played by Affleck’s Justice League co-star Ray Fisher ). Mark and Abigail get a call from an unknown man who reveals that he’s kidnapped their son Denny (Christopher Woodley) and demands a $7 million ransom, money they don’t have on hand because it’s all tied up in Mark’s self-funded campaign. In their desperation, they agree to Mark’s campaign manager Sam’s (Steven Yeun) idea of bringing in mysterious fixer Dayle Burton (Gillian Anderson), who can procure the ransom money (with additional fees involved, of course). The stone-cold, all-business Dayle commences schooling Mark and Abigail on how to deal with the kidnapper while also debunking any illusions they may have about human nature and moral stances. The film’s big twist – which I will not reveal here – spins the movie into a far more compelling direction, both plot-wise and thematically. Until that point, Animals was an engaging flick, but it wasn’t doing anything much different from what we’ve already seen in other kidnapping movies like Ransom (i.e., who can you trust, who is the kidnapper, lots of harrowing phone calls, etc). But the twist then triggers a host of moral quandaries for Mark and Abigail to wrestle with while also forcing them to confront bitter truths about each other and their relationship. Affleck and Washington make their characters three-dimensional, flawed people. Both Mark and Abigail can be hypocritical and selfish at times, and have been unable to speak plainly about their problems with each other until this unthinkable crime happens. They hit each other with some hard truths, and the actors do a good job of capturing the strains in the marriage. Animals takes place after the fires that devastated LA in 2025, and that palpable anger against the political establishment, and how the haves and have-nots have fared since, is a key factor in the film. While Animals reflects the city’s socioeconomic layers and diverse populace, LA is used here as a microcosm of the US for a broader thematic and political commentary about the rich and the poor and American citizens and undocumented immigrants. All said, Animals gets pretty bleak and cynical in its depiction of human nature and the price of victory.
items.title_en: Animals Review

items.title: Smile 2 Star Kyle Gallner Wants to Play V in Paramount’s Cyberpunk 2077 Movie
items.excerpt: Smile 2 star Kyle Gallner is making it known that he’s ready and willing to play V in Paramount’s film adaptation of Cyberpunk 2077.
items.content_text: Smile 2 star Kyle Gallner is making it known that he’s ready and willing to play V in Paramount’s live-action film adaptation of Cyberpunk 2077. Cyberpunk 2077 has come a long way from its roots as a tabletop RPG. Thanks to CD Projekt Red’s video game and its standout expansion, as well as the critically-acclaimed Edgerunners spinoff anime from Studio Trigger, fans of the gritty sci-fi series are eating well. They’re about to get fed even more, as Paramount revealed that it is developing a live-action movie based on the franchise. Thus far, we’re not sure of any plot details, so it’s possible that we could follow V’s adventures with Johnny Silverhand, or Idris Elba’s Solomon Reed before he meets V — or heck, maybe even Edgerunner 2’s Weak Kingsley, for all we know! What we do know is that there’s no shortage of possibilities for this film, and that’s what has fans so excited. One of these fans is none other than actor Kyle Gallner, who is raring to step into Night City as the male version of V. Mere hours after Paramount announced the news on October 8, Gallner posted a photo of himself sporting a close-shaved crop of hair, similar to V’s hairstyle in the game’s marketing materials, along with the caption: “Take me to night city.” It’s safe to say that fans are pretty enthusiastic about this possible casting, with many already envisioning Gallner alongside Keanu Reeves’ Johnny Silverhand. Take me to night city. https://t.co/qchq61ZW9P — Kyle Gallner (@KyleGallner) October 8, 2026 “Kyle and Keanu. Sounds outstanding,” one wrote, while another said Gallner would be “PERFECT casting.” “You and Keanu teaming up? I could be on board for that,” another commented. “He’s HIM! Paramount, please consider,” yet another vouched. For now, details about the movie are being kept under wraps, but CDPR co-CEO Michał Nowakowski promised that more information will come soon. "We're excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise," he said on X. "We look forward to sharing more details at the appropriate time." While they wait for more news, fans can look forward to Edgerunners 2 , set to air on Netflix on October 20, 2026. Image Credits: Araya Doheny/Getty Images for SAG-AFTRA Foundation
items.title_en: Smile 2 Star Kyle Gallner Wants to Play V in Paramount’s Cyberpunk 2077 Movie

items.title: Princess Donut Blind Box Plushies Are Getting Shown Off at NYCC Alongside Dungeon Crawler Carl Action Figures
items.excerpt: The Dungeon Crawler Carl series has absolutely blown up this year. Matt Dinniman's LitRPG story has created some truly dedicated fans who are showing up in droves to support DCC as it transitions to a major franchise.
items.content_text: The Dungeon Crawler Carl series has absolutely blown up this year. Matt Dinniman's LitRPG story has created some truly dedicated fans who are showing up in droves to support DCC as it transitions to a major franchise. IGN's Blythe Dujardin is on the ground at NYCC this week and can confirm that Dungeon Crawler Carl is there in force this year. Most notably, all of the new action figures and toys were on full display at the show. We even got a closer look at three of the Princess Donut plushies that come in the upcoming blind box. The Princess Posse Plush Blind Boxes were first announced back at the end of August , but we haven't gotten much more information about them since then. You can currently preorder these blind boxes directly from EBGames Canada for $19.99 with an October 30 release date. According to information from the product page, each blind box includes one Princess Donut plush with a total of six different variations available. There doesn't seem to be a U.S.-based listing available yet, so it's unclear when you can expect them to drop in the states. With the sudden rise in popularity, the merch side of the franchise is still trying to catch up. Playmates announced a new line of DCC action figures back in February , for example, but they are still rolling those out to major retailers this month. The very popular Dungeon Crawler Carl tabletop games are still a couple months away, as well. The incredibly successful crowdfunding campaign wrapped up in May with just over $13 million raised for the project , which has likely sped up production, but we're still looking at a December release date for the commercial product. With the Dungeon Crawler Carl TV series in the works at Peacock and two more books still on the way, this is likely only the first wave of DCC merch we'll see over the years. If you haven't already read the books, you can check out our guide to the series for more information.
items.title_en: Princess Donut Blind Box Plushies Are Getting Shown Off at NYCC Alongside Dungeon Crawler Carl Action Figures

items.title: Street Fighter 6 Producer Reveals How He Helped Save Capcom’s Iconic Fighting Game Franchise From ‘Dying’
items.excerpt: Street Fighter 6 producer Shuhei Matsumoto revealed how dire things were for Capcom’s flagship fighting game franchise during the Street Fighter V era and explained how he and director Takayuki Nakayama worked together to save the series from death.
items.content_text: Street Fighter 6 producer Shuhei Matsumoto revealed how dire things were for Capcom’s flagship fighting game franchise during the Street Fighter V era and explained how he and director Takayuki Nakayama worked together to save the series from death. It’s no secret that Street Fighter V stumbled massively when it launched in February 2016. Many players felt that it was shipped out in an unfinished state, as it lacked basic elements like an arcade mode or story mode, on top of its incredibly unstable netplay. Shuhei Matsumoto — who stepped in as producer for Street Fighter V near the end of its lifetime following Yoshinori Ono’s exit from Capcom in 2020 — alongside director Takayuki Nakayama, recognized that the franchise as a whole was in peril, and believed that the Street Fighter IP might actually fade into obscurity within the next decade if they didn’t act fast. "When the two of us were talking during Street Fighter V, we realized that if we didn't do something about Street Fighter, the Street Fighter IP would probably die in 10 years. It was critical. So, we had to make it a game where people would get to know it all over again and play it again,” Matsumoto said during an October 2026 interview with Karin Ohira . Matsumoto explained that SFV’s aging playerbase was one example of this issue, saying Capcom needed to target younger players if it wanted Street Fighter to live. "At that time, the player base for Street Fighter V was roughly 35 to 45 years old. In 10 years, these people will be 60. It’s difficult to sustain the franchise if we only rely on that group,” he continued. "...It had become a distant presence. People knew of the scene, but weren't actually playing the game, which made us think, 'This is bad.' In the end, we're a game company, yet people weren't playing our game. Isn't that the most fatal thing? So that was the biggest danger. We didn't know if those people would continue with the same level of passion, and naturally, there's a lifespan to things, right? That's when we talked about how, if we left it as it was, the IP would likely die in 10 years." So, how did they manage to turn things around so dramatically with Street Fighter 6 ? Matsumoto said that the team avoided relying on its power as a historic IP, and decided to start with a blank slate, as if no one in the current generation knew about it, at all. "While people say Street Fighter has high name recognition, we shouldn't be overconfident. We decided to act as if the current generation doesn't know us. We have to properly explain things to those who are just starting to play games now — like who these characters are and how to play — so we don't take that familiarity for granted." Matsumoto also said that the development of SF6's Modern control scheme was integral to reaching a new audience, alongside other approachable features like World Tour Mode (which has since been paused for the forseeable future), the Battle Hub, and real-time commentary from community figures like Vicious and Tasty Steve. Matsumoto and Nakayama’s plan paid off big time; Street Fighter 6 is one of Capcom’s most successful Street Fighter games of all time, having sold more than seven million lifetime units as of summer 2026. It’s extremely popular both in Japan and abroad, and boasts a massive playerbase across both Steam and consoles. It’s a big year for Street Fighter fans and Capcom in general; the developer has released three critically-acclaimed titles in Resident Evil Requiem , Pragmata , and Onimusha: Way of the Sword , and is gearing up for the Street Fighter movie on October 16, which comes on the heels of the Resident Evil adaptation directed by horror savant Zach Cregger.
items.title_en: Street Fighter 6 Producer Reveals How He Helped Save Capcom’s Iconic Fighting Game Franchise From ‘Dying’

items.title: Ben Affleck Says He Gets Into Arguments With Kids in Fortnite, His New Movie Took Inspiration from Game's Skins
items.excerpt: Ben Affleck has revealed he plays shooters like Fortnite and sometimes ends up getting into arguments with kids in voice chat.
items.content_text: Ben Affleck has revealed he plays shooters like Fortnite and sometimes ends up getting into arguments with kids in voice chat. When speaking on the New Heights podcast , Affleck was asked about the inspiration for some of the costumes in his latest film, Animals. The new Netflix thriller features a character wearing a fuzzy bunny mask, and Affleck stated that he took inspiration from Fortnite for that particular costume. He noted that his son was taking an interest in Fortnite skins and kept calling them "tough." Affleck joked that he didn't quite understand what was "tough" about a character wearing a bunny mask, but utilized it as an inspiration. "I thought these costumes are so kind of random and unusual, that's what I based the costumes on," said Affleck. "I thought he'd be getting them off games." The actor also noted that he plays quite a few games himself, including sports titles like Madden and 2K, as well as shooters. Affleck joked that because of his gaming experience, he believes he's good at shooters, but realizes he's not as capable as younger players. "I always play games," he said. "I play first person shooter games, so I think I'm good, and then 12-year-olds just f**k you up. I try to come out and I'm like, ‘Here I come.’ I get killed right away, and then they taunt you, like, ‘You suck. F**k you!’ I end up getting in arguments. ‘F**k you! I don't suck! I'm a grown man!’” Affleck has been vocal about his love for gaming before, particularly Valorant. The actor has attended multiple Valorant events with his son, noting in the past that he mains KAY/0 in the game. He also joined the Valorant e-Sports team Sentinels for a watch party last year , where he talked about his experience with the game on stream.
items.title_en: Ben Affleck Says He Gets Into Arguments With Kids in Fortnite, His New Movie Took Inspiration from Game's Skins

items.title: Deadpool and She-Hulk Are Coming to X-Men '97 Season 3
items.excerpt: We've already known that X-Men '97 Season 3 was happening, but at New York Comic Con 2026, Marvel showed the first teaser for the new season, with surprise appearances from Deadpool and She-Hulk.
items.content_text: We've already known that X-Men '97 Season 3 was happening, but at New York Comic Con 2026, Marvel showed the first teaser for the new season, with surprise appearances from Deadpool and She-Hulk. After the chaotic ending of Season 2, the X-Men are scattered, and according to Variety, the trailer shows Deadpool and She-Hulk in attendance of Rogue and Gambit's wedding – which is also a thing, apparently. From this brief appearnace, it's not clear how big of a role either of these characters will play. It's possible that they're just in a brief cameo for the wedding. However, Deadpool is no stranger to working with the X-Men when it suits him, so we could totally see him having a bigger part. We don't know much else about what X-Men '97 season 3 is going to be about yet, though. Back at SDCC, Marvel revealed some clips of the Brotherhood of Mutants, with Pyro, Avalanche, Toad, and Blob writing "mutant freedom" on the side of a building. Then, of course, they're attacked by a sentinel dressed in red, white, and blue paint. But while we knew that the Brotherhood of Mutants is back, we also know who is leading them after Magneto's death at the hands of Apocalypse in season 2. The trailer shows Mystique leading the team, which opens up a ton of possibilities. Luckily, during the SDCC panel, Executive Producer Brad Winderbaum suggested that the studio was wrapping up animation on season 3 while season 2 was finishing. Hopefully that, combined with this new trailer, means that season 3 will come out sometime next year. But we'll just have to wait for Marvel to reveal more information.
items.title_en: Deadpool and She-Hulk Are Coming to X-Men '97 Season 3

items.title: Resident Evil Requiem Was Originally Planned as an Online Game, Producer Says
items.excerpt: Resident Evil Requiem producer Masachika Kawata revealed that the game was originally planned to be an online title before they scrapped the idea to focus on horror.
items.content_text: Resident Evil Requiem producer Masachika Kawata revealed that the game was originally planned to be an online title before they scrapped the idea to focus on horror. Kawata shared this information in the Biohazard 30th Special Mook (‘magazine book’), a 124-page, full-color fan book with a complete history of the series' timeline, creature genealogy, and developer interviews. “Every game is a continuous process of trial and error. For example, with Resident Evil Requiem, [game director Koshi Nakanishi] initially went so far as to develop it as an online game,” he said, via a fan translation. “However, the results of research conducted partway through development were not favorable, so we decided to prioritize the horror concept once again and abandoned the online direction.” That’s not the only wild thing Kawata revealed in the mook; he also said that Leon was the first character the team chose as a protagonist, but they ultimately felt that being able to hack and slash zombies with ease would lean too heavily on the "action" side of things, making the overall game less scary. “Leon was also the first character confirmed to appear as a protagonist. However, we determined that with Leon alone, who excels in combat, ‘horror would no longer work,’ so it was decided to introduce Grace as a new character,” he continued. Kawata also explained why Capcom decided to wait before sharing Leon’s involvement in the game, saying, “By keeping the full picture of the game, which would develop along both the horror and action sides, until the very end, we were able to successfully maintain interest in it up until release.” Nakanishi’s early plans to make RE9 an online game isn’t something totally surprising, given that management at Capcom had also pushed for Resident Evil 7 to have multiplayer and microtransactions during its conceptual phase. "Right around that time, there was a big push at Capcom, a big 'marketing' push, saying 'we have to make the games players are asking for,'" franchise producer Jun Takeuchi said in 2022. "So we were being told 'make this, make that', it was really hard on the directors at the time. 'Online multiplayer' this, 'downloadable content' that. 'Ongoing service games! Microtransactions! Make a Resident Evil game that ticks all those boxes!' “The idea of multiplayer got killed off pretty quickly. If we could properly put it together, we could make an exciting horror multiplayer game, but we didn’t really have any good ideas, so we set it aside. We went down the list, chopping them out, until we had marketing’s worst nightmare — a regular old single-player horror game." Capcom is moving full speed ahead with many of its high-profile IPs, Resident Evil being one of them. The series just enjoyed a film adaptation directed by Zach Cregger, and a Code Veronica remake is set to release in February next year. Given that the devs of RE9 didn’t move forward with an online version of the game, it’s possible that we see another online Resident Evil title in the future — perhaps another Resident Evil Outbreak?

items.title: Jessica Chastain Reveals the ‘Painful’ Secret to her Terrifying Smile in Other Mommy
items.excerpt: Jessica Chastain explained how she pulled off the terrifying facial expression she makes as the Other Mommy, saying that physical “pain” was a central part of getting her uncanny smile just right.
items.content_text: Jessica Chastain explained how she pulled off the terrifying facial expression she makes in the Other Mommy, saying that physical “pain” was a central part of getting her uncanny smile just right. Chastain stars in Universal Pictures’ Other Mommy , where she plays both the mother of a young girl and the entity that haunts her family. It’s a Coraline-style premise that adds another horror film to her steadily-growing roster of projects in the genre ( IT Chapter 2 , Mama, Crimson Peak ). The big draw for this film is Chastain’s horrifying transformation from a caring mother to a bloodthirsty entity wearing her skin. Trailers for the movie show the acclaimed actress in both roles; when she plays the entity, she wears a dead-eyed expression with a wide, almost painful-looking smile. It turns out that this smile does, indeed, channel some element of physical pain, as told by Chastain during an appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live where she explained how she came up with the entity’s distinct facial expression. “I thought about this entity holding on the skin of a person, and maybe that’s the painful thing, like maybe you’re holding a box for a long time that’s very heavy. So the tension in your body, you have to hold this, and then, you have to smile, because you need a child to think you’re safe and approachable,” she said. She then demonstrated the smile for the audience and even shed a tear right on cue. It was an impressive display of her acting ability, which Kimmel pointed out once her demo was done. “I am a trained actress,” she joked. “You know what it is? I really felt the pain in my body, and that’s why, sometimes, you can see in the neck in the pictures — but then try to be as nice as possible. Don’t show your teeth.” Thus far, early reviews for Other Mommy have been rather merciless ; viewers who’ve seen it ahead of its October 9 theatrical release have called it “more silly than it is scary,” “truly dreadful,” and “masterfully cringe” on social media. Viewers will have to judge for themselves when the film comes out tomorrow. For now, we can hope that Chastain’s impressive acting carries Other Mommy. That smile is certainly unsettling all on its own! Image Credits - YouTube: Jimmy Kimmel Live

items.title: Xbox XP's First Task Should Be the Halo Movie We Never Got
items.excerpt: Microsoft has just announced Xbox XP, a new division aimed at getting cool experiences – be they movies, TV shows, theme park attractions, etc. – made out of its many intellectual properties. And that's how Microsoft can erase the memory of the TV show you probably already forgot anyway. No, I'm not suggesting that they necessarily dust off Garland's 20-year-old script (unless it's awesome, then by all means, do it!), but by turning Halo into the movie we deserve but never got.
items.content_text: Halo should've never ended up as a mid-at-best TV show on Paramount Plus. Instead of " Master Cheeks ," we should've gotten a big-budget big-screen feature film with Xbox's halo-nuking helmeted hero. And that was the plan. Guys dressed up as Master Chief even delivered 28 Days Later scribe Alex Garland's script to various movie studios as Microsoft tried to sell the film to the highest bidder. But things went how they went . Now, however, Microsoft has just announced Xbox XP , a new division aimed at getting cool experiences – be they movies, TV shows, theme park attractions, etc. – made out of its many intellectual properties. And that's how Microsoft can erase the memory of the TV show you probably already forgot anyway. No, I'm not suggesting that they necessarily dust off Garland's 20-year-old script (unless it's awesome, then by all means, do it!), but by turning Halo into the movie we deserve but never got. Sure, TV shows are great because they're often cheaper than films and can be stretched out over multiple years, potentially sustaining added interest in the brand longer than a single-pop movie would. But short of making something legendary on the level of Breaking Bad or The Sopranos, the ceiling is a lot lower on a TV show than on a movie, which could make a billion dollars if executed correctly. It's not that Halo can't work as a TV show (despite Paramount Plus's evidence to the contrary), it's just that Halo is a game with the right combination of lore, action, and established cultural cachet that it would be best served as a big-budget movie. And finding the right people to make exactly that should be Xbox XP's first order of business. Canon doesn't really matter for a movie, because a major motion picture should probably just tell the story of the legendary first game. Not only because it's a great story, but because it's already tailor-made for a three-act movie. We start where the game does, waking up Master Chief from cryosleep aboard the Pillar of Autumn as the Covenant attack. Chief steps out, kicks a bunch of ass, and then there's time to fill in some backstory and do a bit of character intros for Chief, Cortana, and the Spartan program with Dr. Halsey. Then we head down to the Halo ring, mix some Covenant backstory in with more action, and then the non-gamer audience gets surprised with the introduction of The Flood (it'd be important to not give away that twist in the trailers), before things escalate in the third act as Chief and Cortana destroy the whole damn thing. Look, I'm obviously no scriptwriter, but my point is that the first priority of Xbox XP should be getting Halo on the big screen. The franchise is in a state of metamorphosis as it is, with Activision now taking on responsibility for development of the next mainline game . With a team being spun up and probably plugged into the efficient Call of Duty pipeline pretty soon, my money is on Activision shipping its first big Halo game in four years. It could be three and it probably won't be five, knowing that Sharma wants Halo back in the marketplace, so my money's on four (with three-year development cycles after that, but we can talk about that another time ). My point is: that's plenty of time to get a Halo movie together, and perhaps even launch them together for the Ultimate Corporate Synergy™ that new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma would no doubt love to see. This is a franchise that has had names like Stephen Spielberg and Peter Jackson attached to it at various points over the years. And fortunately, finding talented people to put a Halo movie together shouldn't be a problem. After all, this is a franchise that, in addition to the aforementioned and accomplished Garland, has also had names like Stephen Spielberg and Peter Jackson attached to it at various points over the years. Halo as a whole is in desperate need of a turnaround, whether it's rebounding from the abandoned two-season Paramount Plus show or bouncing back from an up-and-down couple of decades under the stewardship of 343 Industries/Halo Studios. We'll see what Activision can do on the games side of things, but it's up to Xbox XP to show the world how serious they are about this new division by turning Halo into the blockbuster movie it was always meant to be.
items.title_en: Xbox XP's First Task Should Be the Halo Movie We Never Got

items.title: Matchbox The Movie Review
items.excerpt: Matchbox The Movie is glitzy, glossy and hollow, never even trying to present something original. Everything is safe and familiar and easy, which has always been Hollywood's go-to answer for trying to hit as many quadrants as possible, thus potentially making the most money.
items.content_text: Matchbox The Movie premieres October 9 on Apple TV. It's hard separating the cars from the cartist here. Matchbox The Movie starts as a ridiculous ad for the 70-year-old toy line, which are literally just small die-cast metal cars, and then cranks up its volume for some empty, fleeting nonsense. Apple TV has a strong case for having the best quality shows of the Streaming Wars but it's not perfect. Like other streamers, it's also given us dumb bullshit. Let's dig deeper... Sadly, the best thing about Matchbox The Movie -- which is that it goes overboard with large-scale, globe-trotting action -- is hamstrung by it being a watch at home on your couch affair. Look, it's all forgettable, and a waste of a Marvel movie-sized budget, but at least on the big screen the big set pieces from director Sam Hargrave (stunt coordinator for Infinity War and Endgame, director of both Extraction* flicks for Netflix) could get the presentation everyone's hard work deserves. Nothing's ever going to take your breath away on a 55" screen though. (*Despite them also being non-theatrical releases, y'all should check out the insane Oners in this franchise.) Matchbox The Movie centers on middle school friends in a small Ohio town, who call themselves the Matchbox Gang (ugh) because they somehow enjoy playing with teensy cars in the year of our lord 1997. Four of them grow up to have careers based on the specific Matchbox vehicle they liked as a kid (you can almost hear the Mattel boardroom execs hubbub positively at this idea). One of the gang, however, Sean, moves away and winds up becoming a no-ties, family-doesn't-exist dickhead secret agent. John Cena plays adult Sean, who returns home after decades and inadvertently gets his estranged pals roped up in a dangerous international conspiracy involving a missing nuke. Now they all must work together to clear their names and save the day. Jessica Biel, Teyonah Parris, Sam Richardson, and Arturo Castro round out the cast, along with Danai Gurira, and Corey Stoll. None of these folks are to blame here. They're all fun, talented performers more or less wasted in a movie that feels like it came from an episode of The Studio (also available on Apple TV). It just makes you feel bad when these guys do their best to make the movie's meager emotional moments work. "Matchbox is glitzy, glossy and hollow, never even trying to present something original. These aren't really characters, though, they're brief character summaries. Construction truck guy never wants to leave town. His flying wife wants to see the world. Paramedic race car woman wants to help people. And quickly. Fun fact: Since race car lady (Biel) is the woman Cena's spy dude has been pining for, she has to be available. But it's been decades so she had to have been married before. I thought to myself, "I bet she says I was married, didn't take ." And guess what, you guys? Matchbox is glitzy, glossy and hollow, never even trying to present something original. Everything is safe and familiar and easy, which has always been Hollywood's go-to answer for trying to hit as many quadrants as possible, thus potentially making the most money. But it's always, no matter how many times the lesson hasn't been learned, led to unexceptional dust. You also can't trick people into thinking your movie is good by having your characters recurrently reference better action movies. There's a chance this will be a disposable "streaming hit." Like a Red Notice or a Back in Action or a War Machine. It's a futile accolade, based on metrics with too many loopholes, workarounds, and sleight of hand. It means people will put this on their TV, on a service they already subscribe to. It could be on in the background or it could provide TV light while falling asleep. What it definitely means is that people will easily do that rather than buy a ticket to see it in the theater. Let's talk about what this is: it's a multi-million dollar mistake based on the worst takeaways from the massive success of the Barbie movie . It was movie studio and toy company heads thinking that Barbie was a hit because it was based on doll people know. There could be no other reason, right, that people, primarily women, went and saw Barbie over and over again? Here now stands the grotesque love child of this obtuse reasoning. There were then pitches all over town for toy movies. What can we do with Matchbox? The answer is, obviously, nothing. Now, I firmly believe that this film was probably the best idea for a Matchbox movie. But the best idea for a Matchbox movie is still a terrible idea for a movie. If something's the best-worst, or the least-awful, don't make it. Ultimately, any movie based on a toy or a video game or a comic is an ad for that product. Barbie worked because it magically side-stepped that puddle by being about something socially relevant and important. Matchbox was never ever going to be capable of that. Barbie was also damn funny. This movie has laughs you can count on one hand if you're feeling charitable (all, in part, thanks to Sam Richardson). Matchbox The Movie is like when Wayne's World had to shill for Noah's Arcade. There's even a moment in the beginning where a character muses about the history of the Matchbox toy line, like it's Americana we should salute.
items.title_en: Matchbox The Movie Review

items.title: Original Sketch of MrBeast's Logo to Be Auctioned Off With Estimated Value of $20,000
items.excerpt: The original pencil sketch of Jimmy ‘MrBeast’ Donaldson’s famous logo is being auctioned off, and experts estimate that it could be worth over $20,000.
items.content_text: UPDATE: IGN has been informed that MrBeast is not involved with the sale of this pencil sketch, and we have amended our article to reflect this information. The original pencil sketch of Jimmy ‘MrBeast’ Donaldson’s famous logo is being auctioned off, and experts estimate that it could be worth over $20,000. MrBeast is basically synonymous with YouTube these days, and it’s not hard to see why; he’s the single most-subscribed individual creator on the platform (520 million), famous for his over-the-top challenge videos, eye-popping cash prizes, and massive philanthropic projects. Fourteen years after starting his channel in 2012, one of the ideas that has made him a household name is being put up for auction — the very first pencil sketch of his iconic blue tiger logo. It adorns every bit of MrBeast’s branding, from his YouTube channel to his merchandise and even his very own chocolate bar line. Of course, this particular sketch doesn’t have any coloring, but shows the tiger (or, here, a leopard or spotted cat of some kind) as we know it today, minus the pink lightning bolt over its eye. The 8.5-by-11-inch drawing is being put up for bidding as part of Heritage Auctions’ October 23 – 25 Fall Sports Catalog Auction. Experts estimate that, thanks to MrBeast’s mind-blowing net worth and prestige as a content creator, this simple sketch could be worth $20,000 or more. Reps at Heritage Auctions explained that this logo was created around 2018 during a quick, 10-minute brainstorming session. Speaking with Wired , Donaldson explained how he first came up with the design, admitting that “even though that logo has probably been seen a hundred billion times, I actually put very little thought into it.” “When I was a little kid I just kind of designed a tiger, and here we are,” he said. “My name, my logo, probably should have had more thought behind it, I’ll admit it.” He also revealed that even he “doesn’t really know” what type of big cat the animal in his logo is supposed to be. “I guess it’s kind of like a tiger,” he told Wired, though the early concept art being sold at auction suggests that it was initially supposed to be a leopard or panther of some kind. MrBeast has grown from his roots as a viral YouTuber into a fully-fledged game show host with his own series on Amazon’s Prime Video, Beast Games . It's got two seasons that are available to watch right now, and has been renewed for a third one. He has also co-authored a book with Alex Cross writer James Patterson called The Most Dangerous Games, which, as you can probably guess, follows 100 strangers who enter a contest for the chance of winning a billion dollars. Image Credits: Instagram: MrBeast

items.title: Backrooms on 4K UHD and Blu-ray Is Up for Preorder at Amazon
items.excerpt: The psychological horror movie Backrooms is getting a home release in November, when it hits 4K UHD Blu-ray for the first time.
items.content_text: Here’s one for fans of horror movies or liminal spaces in general. Backrooms , the major motion picture based on a concept that originated as an internet creepypasta, is up for preorder on Amazon on 4K UHD and Blu-ray . It's an A24 release, and it comes with six collectible postcards. It will be released on November 17. Preoder Backrooms (4K UHD Blu-ray) Get it on 4K UHD - $35 Get it on Blu-ray - $30 Rent or Buy on Prime Video - $7.99 or 19.99 Backrooms stars Chiwetel Ejiofor, Renate Reinsve, and Mark Duplass, and not many other people. It’s a spare film that moves slowly yet assuredly through its unsettling narrative. Ejiofor plays a down-on-his-luck furniture store manager who discovers that the basement of the store contains a portal into a strange, seemingly alternate world. Special Features “Everything Must Go” Bonus Footage Commentary with Director Kane parsons, VFX Supervisor Edward J Douglas, Sound Designer Eugenio Battaglia, and Composer Edo Van Breemen “Building the Backrooms” Featurette Scene Breakdown with Kane Parsons Prop Walkthrough with Kane Parsons VFX Breakdowns Six Collectible Postcards The portal leads to a seemingly endless string of connected yellow rooms and hallways, all lit by fluorescent lights and designed with weird and off-putting architecture. There are nooks and crannies where none should be, and half-walls and items from the outside world placed haphazardly in nonsensical locations. The rooms also seem to be home to a violent creature lurking in the shadows. I watched it recently when it debuted on HBO , and I can attest it’s an unsettling movie that goes some very strange places. It was directed by Kane Parsons, and based partially on a series of YouTube videos he filmed and uploaded starting in 2022. This movie is Parsons’ directorial debut, and according to Wikipedia , “At age 20, Parsons became the youngest director to have a film debut at number one at both the domestic and global box offices, with Backrooms grossing over $400 million worldwide.” In IGN’s Backrooms review , critic Lex Briscuso wrote, “Backrooms expertly expands on the conceptual groundwork of the YouTube series with smart visual composition, beautifully terrifying production design, a complex protagonist, and a return to Kane Parsons’ roots of computer generated sequences that pack a serious punch.” For more, check out our full list of all the biggest upcoming 4K UHD and Blu-ray release dates .
